text:
anita (PM): ok kicking off a quick thread to align scope for the next quarter: chat + embeddings surface. need a tight set of launch guards and clear SLAs before we commit to the slice. thoughts?

sam (Eng Lead): +1. main tradeoffs: batching vs latency, model family (mix small fast vs larger quality), and embedding dim/encoder cost. we should pick a primary SLAs target and one rollback trigger.

mike (ML): suggested OKR: "improve chat median latency while keeping generation quality delta <2% on customer evals". For embeddings, we should standardize to 1536 dims for now to simplify rerank pipeline unless customers push for 3072.

jordan (Prod-Ops): we need concrete launch guards. propose:
- canary at 5% traffic for 48h
- p95 token latency < 350ms on canary or auto-fallback to smaller model
- embedding cosine similarity drift < 0.02 vs baseline on a fixed probe set

anita (PM): those are good. add cost cap per 1M tokens for hosted tier. customers asked for predictable unit economics. also we should list minimal telemetry for shipped product.

eva (Data): telemetry checklist: token-level latency histogram, per-model quality deltas on evaluation set (weekly), embedding distribution summaries and drift alerts, rerank accuracy (MRR) trending. We can wire these into console dashboards.

sam (Eng Lead): for rollout plan:
```
canary_config:
  percent: 5
  duration: 48h
  monitors:
    - p95_token_latency < 350ms
    - error_rate < 0.5%
    - embedding_drift < 0.02
fallback_policy: route_to_small_model
```
If any monitor trips, we auto-fallback and page oncall.

mike (ML): also recommend an offline "quality gate" before canary: run our eval harness (1000 prompts across customers) comparing candidate model -> baseline. auto-fail if ROUGE/QA metric drop > 1.5% or hallucination rate increases.

anita (PM): scope decisions to make now: 1) embedding dim (1536 vs 3072) 2) include rerank in launch or ship as separate opt-in? 3) model variants to expose for hosted free tier vs paid. please vote quick: react with :one: for 1536, :two: for 3072. react :one: for rerank later, :two: for rerank in launch. :one: to expose only small/medium on free tier, :two: to expose large as opt-in.

(eva reacts with :one:)
(sam reacts with :one:)
(mike reacts with :two:)

jordan reacts with :one:)

sam (Eng Lead): based on reactions, defaulting to 1536, rerank as opt-in post-launch, free tier gets small/medium only. I'll sketch capacity numbers.

jordan (Prod-Ops): capacity estimates: assume peak qps 250 for initial canary. with batching we need ~6 GPUs for canary on small models, 18 for canary if we include medium/large. need final numbers from runtime team.

mike (ML): note on embedding drift guard: we need a stable probe set and weekly scheduled evaluation. eva can own probe set; i'll add hooks in eval harness.

anita (PM): launch criteria (proposed short list):
- telemetry wired to console + alerts
- canary run 48hrs with no critical trips and quality gate pass
- cost per 1M tokens within target bands (pm/sales agreed)
- docs + SDK examples for rerank + recommended prompt patterns
- rollback plan tested

jordan (Prod-Ops): add: monitoring for prefix cache hit-rate and batch size distribution. if average batch_size < 1.8 we won't auto-enable batching.

mike (ML): small note: consider shipping a "quality-mode" knob that pins quantization / beam settings to preserve deterministic output for some customers. low lift and helps enterprise asks.

anita (PM): agree. assign owners and dates? propose next steps:
- sam: capacity & runtime changes (ETA 2w)
- mike: eval harness + quality gate (ETA 1w)
- eva: probe set + telemetry schema (ETA 1w)
- jordan: canary runbook + alerts (ETA 1w)
- anita: doc outline + pricing constraints (ETA 2w)

sam (Eng Lead): I'll post a short PR with capacity numbers and config.

jordan (Prod-Ops): will draft canary runbook then ping oncall for dry-run.

deploy-bot: scheduled deployment window created: 1758945600 -> canary window placeholder.

anita (PM): thanks all. we'll reconvene in async check-in next Tue. if any objections to scope, raise them here. :rocket:
